PBS Frontline Program Snitch Gives Devastating Critique Of Drug War
On Both Television And The Internet

As indicated by the title, the primary focus was on the Federal prosecutors’ use of their discretion in sentencing under the extremely harsh mandatory minimums to extort perjurious testimony from defendants.

It is not just the crime bosses who make offers that people can’t refuse: "Name -- frame -- others, or go to prison for life."

The program also illustrated the abuses of forfeiture laws and their disproportionate impact on African Americans.
See
Public Health Reports Journal Says Prohibition Increases Harm Done By Drugs;
Burden Falls Disproportionately On Blacks - "The cure has only worsened the disease."

Short interviews with arch-prohibitionists like Florida Representative McCallum and Utah Senator Hatch – as well as a Georgia Federal Prosecutor who is a Bob Barr clone – gave a frightening insight into the mindset of those who think that the end justifies the means.

McCollum actually says, "Good Lord, informants are a way of life in American justice whether it's a drug case or not. How else are we going to find the bad guy?"

The program also continued Frontline’s groundbreaking combination of television and the Internet. During the program, frequent banners appeared on the screen reminding viewers that they can learn more by visiting the PBS.org web site.

I urge you to do so now. There is a wealth of information at
http://www.pbs.org/wgbh/pages/frontline/shows/snitch/

As I love to say, the drug war cannot survive this kind of journalism.

Bravo!!
